 INDIA STOCKS-Indian shares open lower as oil surge, inflation jitters weigh
 (Updates for markets open)- Indian equity benchmarks opened lower on Friday, consolidating after recent gains, as elevated crude prices and inflationary pressures weighed on 
 Reuters 
 Published On Nov 13, 2026 at 09:40 AM IST

 (Updates for markets open)
- Indian equity benchmarks opened lower on Friday, consolidating after recent gains, as elevated crude prices and inflationary pressures weighed on sentiment, countering the support from sustained foreign institutional inflows.
The Nifty 50 was down 0.35% at 25,209.85 and the Sensex edged 0.09% lower to 81,833.78, as of 9:15 a.m. IST.
 All 16 major sector logged losses. The broader small-caps and mid-caps lost 0.2% and 0.3%, respectively.
Foreign investors continued their strong buying streak, recording net purchases of 78.31 billion ($832.71 million) in Indian equities on Thursday, according to provisional data. This marked their ninth consecutive session of net buying. November inflows have already reached $8 billion, the highest monthly tally since December 2020.
 Advt 
 Weighing on sentiment, India's retail inflation accelerated to 6.09% in October, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's upper tolerance of 6%. Rising food prices have squeezed household budgets and fuelled expectations of further monetary tightening.
Brent crude futures traded around $95.5 per barrel, from $92 during India equity market close on Thursday, as attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure escalated and shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz threatened global oil flows.
 (Reporting by Vivek Kumar M and Bharath Rajeswaran; Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips)
